title: Preventing Falling Objects and Struck-By Injuries
summary: Struck-by falling objects is a leading cause of construction deaths. Even a small tool dropped from height can kill. This talk covers securing tools, toeboards, and hard hats.
talking_points: Secure tools in elevated work areas, especially near leading edges. Use a tool lanyard or holster for hand tools.
Secure loads before lifting or moving them with a lift or crane. Do not hoist or pass loads over people.
Stack materials neatly so they cannot topple.
Ask your employer for debris nets or toeboards on scaffolding and open edges to catch tools and material.
Always wear a hard hat and the other PPE for the job.
site_hazards_to_check: Unsecured tools or material near edges, floor openings, or scaffold platforms
Loads carried or swung over workers below
Missing toeboards or debris nets on elevated platforms
Poorly stacked or leaning material piles
Workers below overhead work without hard hats or a barricaded exclusion zone
discussion_questions: What tools and materials are overhead today, and how are they secured?
Where can people walk under overhead work, and should that area be barricaded?
How do you tie off a hand tool when working near a leading edge?

flags: OSHA mapping accurate: 29 CFR 1926.501(c) (falling-object protection duty) and 1926.100 (head protection). Content - secure tools at height / use lanyards and holsters, secure and never suspend loads over people, stack materials so they cannot topple, request toeboards/debris nets, barricade exclusion zones, wear hard hats - is sound.
